testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: While driving, spring brakes are held in place by:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes are held in place by air pressure while driving. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: If you use air tanks with manual drains, how often should you drain them?
questions.explanation: Drain manual air tank drains at the end of each day of driving. This prevents oil and water from building up in the air tanks.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tank.
Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil that build up inside. Not draining them can cause damage. Use manual drains at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: A vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to show the system is not working properly.
questions.explanation: ABS malfunction lamps are usually yellow. Even if the ABS is not working, you will still be able to use your regular brakes.

questions.question: When checking your brakes, a slack adjuster should move ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: After placing wheel chocks and releasing the parking brake, check each slack adjuster. Pull the slack adjusters and make sure they move no more than about one inch from the push rod. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment and repairs.

questions.question: In a static leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes is ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, leakage should not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle should not be driven because repairs are needed.

questions.question: Pressing the brake pedal causes air pressure to activate an electric switch and:

options.text: Turn on the low pressure warning light.
Turn off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, pressing the brake pedal activates an electric switch. Air pressure moves this switch to turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels and located on the vehicle's axles. The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are inside the drum brake.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what do both systems share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work properly.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Engage and disengage the parking brake
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times
Disconnect and reconnect all glad hands

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system fills with air, test the warning by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air, and the warning should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the tank drops below 60 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will not shift out of gear

questions.explanation: In an air brake system, a warning signal activates when air tank pressure falls below 60 psi. The signal may be a warning light or a wig wag.

questions.question: In an emergency stop, what should you do?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop
Stop while keeping the vehicle in a straight line
Expect the vehicle to stop faster than normal

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop while keeping the vehicle in a straight line
questions.explanation: In an emergency, use controlled braking or stab braking. Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle going straight while still allowing you to turn if needed.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When air is pumped into the storage tanks
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks
The temperature of the air being pumped

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the storage tanks
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system have?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. The number and size of tanks varies depending on the vehicle.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Prevent the air compressor from overheating
Prevent using front brakes on ice
Prevent brake use when downshifting would be better

questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking during hard braking, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When do brakes get out of adjustment?
questions.explanation: Brakes can quickly get out of adjustment if they overheat from use. Check brake adjustment frequently.

questions.question: What should you do when using controlled braking in an emergency?

options.text: Brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels
Brake with about half your normal force

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels
questions.explanation: In controlled braking for emergencies, apply maximum braking force without locking the wheels. Keep steering movements small while braking.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: What does the emergency brake system use?

options.text: Only parts from the parking brake system.
Only parts from the service brake system.
Parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
Parts that are only used for the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What do the air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold air for only one brake use.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor fails.
Only hold air during an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 brake uses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in an air brake system hold enough air so the brakes can be used several times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being sent to the brakes.
The temperature of the air in the brake system.
The pressure of air from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being sent to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being sent to the brakes. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what happens?

options.text: The risk of jackknifing goes down.
The risk of jackknifing goes up.
The brakes do not work as well as they would without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risk of jackknifing goes down.
questions.explanation: When a tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, the risk of jackknifing is reduced and the driver can still steer. If only the trailer has ABS, it is less likely to swing out to the side.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal on S-cam brakes, what does the air pressure move?
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal on S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.
